title: Interactional Automatisms in Scientific Communication: A Network-Based Model of Distributed Evaluation

detail.title: Interactional Automatisms in Scientific Communication: A Network-Based Model of Distributed Evaluation
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of global scientific production has created significant challenges for traditional mechanisms of knowledge validation and coordination. As the volume of publications, collaborations, and datasets continues to grow exponentially, sequential peer-review systems increasingly struggle to operate efficiently at the scale of contemporary research ecosystems. This article proposes a theoretical and operational framework for understanding scientific validation as an emergent property of distributed interaction dynamics within research networks.Building on insights from network science, the sociology of science, and complex systems theory, the study introduces the concept of interactional attractors, referring to scientific contributions that concentrate attention and evaluation within the research system. These attractors generate interactional automatisms, self-reinforcing processes through which scientific credibility evolves through distributed interactions among researchers, institutions, and knowledge objects.The article develops a multi-layer analytical framework combining theoretical modeling, empirical case studies, and systemic formalization. Drawing on examples such as accelerated research dynamics during global crises and the increasing dominance of collaborative scientific networks, the analysis illustrates how interactional mechanisms shape the diffusion and evaluation of scientific knowledge.Building on these dynamics, the paper proposes a distributed validation architecture—the PP-Science protocol—capable of integrating multiple evaluation signals including expert assessments, interaction intensity, and network diffusion patterns. Rather than replacing traditional peer-review institutions, the model envisions hybrid infrastructures that combine institutional legitimacy with the adaptive capacity of distributed scientific networks.The results contribute to the emerging field of the science of science by providing a conceptual and systemic framework for analyzing how scientific validation may evolve in large-scale knowledge systems.

title: Bus dwell time estimation based solely on passenger tag-in and tag-out stamps from smart card data
affiliations: Chung-Ang University, Chung-Ang University and Chung-Ang University

detail.title: Bus dwell time estimation based solely on passenger tag-in and tag-out stamps from smart card data
detail.abstract: Predicting bus dwell time is crucial for the advanced operation of bus transit systems. The accuracy of predicting the bus arrival time at a stop depends on the accuracy of bus dwell times at previous stops, and the estimation of bus dwell time governs the bus stop capacity. The bus dwell time estimation technologies are thus a key prerequisite for the advanced bus information system (BIS) and bus management system (BMS). The present study proposes a rigorous bus dwell time estimation model that works under the restrict environment where only smart card data are available which involve tag-in and tag-out time stamps of passengers. Most previous models require observed bus dwell times for calibration, which should be obtained via direct survey or from automatic vehicle location (AVL) system. The present study compensates the data unavailability with the rigorous modelling with stochasticity. The theoretical identification for estimating the model parameters is rigorously proved, and sufficient conditions for empirical identification are presented. The predicted bus dwell times are validated indirectly via the statistical significance and the rationality of parameter estimates and directly against the small amount of surveyed data.

title: ASTF-Net: Geometry-Aware Synchronization of Asynchronous Flight Trajectories for Estimated Time of Arrival Prediction
affiliations: Sichuan University, Sichuan University, Sichuan University, Sichuan University and Imperial College London

detail.title: ASTF-Net: Geometry-Aware Synchronization of Asynchronous Flight Trajectories for Estimated Time of Arrival Prediction

keywords: Estimated Time of Arrival prediction， Asynchronous flight trajectories， Geometry-Aware Deep Learning

detail.abstract: Accurate Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) prediction is vital for Trajectory-Based Operations and eﬃcient runway scheduling. However, real-world Automatic Dependent SurveillanceBroadcast (ADS-B) trajectories exhibit inherent temporal asynchronicity and complex 3D geometric maneuvers, challenging conventional models. This paper proposes the Asynchronous Spatio-Temporal Fusion Network (ASTF-Net) for high-precision ETA forecasting. To faithfully capture physical constraints, we develop a Geometry-Aware Trajectory Encoder (GATE) that explicitly encodes spatial proximity via 3D Earth-Centered, Earth-Fixed (ECEF) coordinates, eﬀectively mitigating spherical distortions. Furthermore, a Dynamic Temporal Attention Network (DTAN) is introduced to natively embed continuous-time dynamics. This explicitly mitigates temporal distortions caused by irregular sampling and radar gaps. For enhanced operational reliability, ASTF-Net utilizes a Laplace-based probabilistic loss to quantify aleatoric uncertainty, providing air traﬃc controllers with critical confidence intervals. Extensive experiments on a large-scale dataset from Beijing Capital International Airport (ICAO: ZBAA), comprising over 110,000 trajectories, demonstrate that ASTF-Net achieves a state-of-the-art MAE of 2.19 minutes. Notably, ablation studies reveal that modeling temporal asynchronicity provides a more decisive inductive bias than merely scaling model depth. The framework oﬀers a robust, eﬃcient solution for synchronized Air Traﬃc Management (ATM).

title: Project portfolio management dynamic capability evolution in large project-based business organizations
affiliations: University of Vaasa and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Project portfolio management dynamic capability evolution in large project-based business organizations
detail.abstract: Project portfolio management (PPM) capability has a strategic role in transforming business operations. Following the fad; like other organizational capabilities, scholars position PPM as a generalizable dynamic capability across all business contexts. Although limited attention has been given to how PPM practices evolve as organizational capability and furthermore assuming its strategic role as a dynamic capability. Our research addresses this gap by discovering PPM evolution through the structures, processes, resources (people), and digital systems of a large project-based business enterprise. The findings reveal distinct routines for portfolio governance, communication, and multi-project management. These routines served the dual purpose of project portfolio management—as both an operational capability and a dynamic capability—within a single large business enterprise. These novel findings contribute to the capability micro-foundation literature and rejuvenate the debate of business context dependent capability evolution. Our PPM evolution synthesis model offers practical guidance for PPM practitioners and broadens the future research avenues on organizational capability development.

title: Operator-Decomposed Dynamic Traffic Assignment for Connected Vehicle Corridors under Directional Demand Shocks

detail.title: Operator-Decomposed Dynamic Traffic Assignment for Connected Vehicle Corridors under Directional Demand Shocks
detail.abstract: Real-time traffic management in connected vehicle corridors becomes particularly challenging when transportation networks are exposed to localized directional demand shocks that generate congestion shockwaves and rapid capacity saturation. Conventional dynamic traffic assignment (DTA) frameworks typically rely on centralized optimization procedures that do not explicitly exploit structural properties of the underlying traffic network, which may lead to unstable routing responses and delayed congestion mitigation under stochastic demand disturbances.,This paper introduces an operator-decomposed dynamic traffic assignment framework for connected vehicle corridors subject to directional demand fluctuations. By representing a bidirectional corridor as a network admitting a discrete reflection symmetry, traffic control actions—including routing guidance and variable speed limits—are decomposed into symmetric and antisymmetric components defined by a network symmetry operator. This transformation enables independent control allocation within orthogonal parity subspaces corresponding to corridor-wide congestion dynamics and directional imbalance dynamics.,We show that when directional demand disturbances primarily excite the antisymmetric traffic mode, operator-aligned control allocation reduces the spectral amplification of congestion perturbations in the closed-loop system. Consequently, the variance of traffic state fluctuations remains bounded by a constant multiple of the disturbance covariance, implying structural suppression of stochastic congestion amplification.,Simulation experiments on a stochastic corridor traffic model demonstrate that the proposed framework substantially improves traffic stability relative to conventional DTA approaches. Peak congestion density is reduced by approximately 18%, average travel time decreases by 16%, and the probability of extreme congestion events is reduced by an order of magnitude. In addition, the operator-decomposed formulation improves numerical conditioning of the control allocation problem, enabling efficient real-time implementation.,These results suggest that exploiting structural symmetries in transportation networks provides a powerful mechanism for stabilizing traffic flows in intelligent transportation systems and may serve as a scalable control paradigm for connected vehicle corridors.

title: Optimal Configuration of Multi-Energy Stations Based on Multi-Dimensional Carbon Compensation and Linear Green Certificate Pricing
affiliations: Yanshan University - Key Laboratory of Power Electronics Energy Conservation and Transmission Control, Yanshan University, Yanshan University and Yanshan University

detail.title: Optimal Configuration of Multi-Energy Stations Based on Multi-Dimensional Carbon Compensation and Linear Green Certificate Pricing

keywords: Carbon emission and green certificate trading

detail.abstract: As energy, carbon, and green certificate markets converge, user-side energy stations have become pivotal to system efficiency and decarbonization. Yet, traditional supply-centric models often ignore the inherent flexibility and market-driven incentives of end-users. This paper bridges that gap by proposing an optimization model for multi-source energy stations, governed by a bilevel Stackelberg game between Integrated Energy Service Providers (IESPs) and user alliances.To guide low-carbon configurations, we first develop a dynamic carbon quota allocation and a stochastic green certificate pricing mechanism grounded in a "value compensation" principle. These elements are integrated into a carbon-certificate mutual assistance framework that reshapes user-side incentives. This synergy is then operationalized through a leader-follower game, where the IESP (leader) and user alliance (follower) navigate market signals to align infrastructure planning with multi-agent interests.Case simulations of a multi-building complex demonstrate that this coordinated approach does more than just ensure economic viability; it actively catalyzes demand-side emission reductions. By aligning equipment selection with market dynamics, the proposed mechanism significantly boosts renewable integration while slashing the total carbon footprint of the end-system.

title: Language-based power in foreign subsidiaries: A three-dimensional power theory perspective

detail.title: Language-based power in foreign subsidiaries: A three-dimensional power theory perspective
detail.abstract: While language has been linked to power in multinational corporations, less is known about how language-based power is developed and maintained in foreign subsidiaries without formal language policies. This study draws on three-dimensional power theory and interviews with 70 expatriates and locally hired parent country nationals to examine collective constructed language-based power in Chinese foreign subsidiaries operating in Japan. The findings suggest that Chinese proficiency provides expatriate and locally hired parent nationals with different forms of decision-making power, non-decision-making power, and ideological power, which marginalize host country employees. This study advances understanding of language as a mechanism of power by demonstrating how language proficiency enables expatriate-locally hired parent country nationals jointly construct and maintain power, control information, and access to decision-makers, and naturalize dominance over host national employees in foreign subsidiaries.

title: ey Factors Influencing Intrafirm Technology Transfer: A Structural Equation Model Approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: ey Factors Influencing Intrafirm Technology Transfer: A Structural Equation Model Approach
detail.abstract: In the global industrial landscape, efficient knowledge absorption and internal technology transfer are critical for competitiveness. This study utilizes Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) to examine organizational constructs influencing Absorptive Capacity and Intrafirm Technology Transfer (IFTT) within 42 manufacturing firms. Results indicate that Organizational Agility, Qualified Human Talent, and Leadership are significant drivers of Absorptive Capacity, with Realized Absorptive Capacity acting as the primary enabler of effective IFTT. Conversely, Knowledge Management and Learning Culture exhibited weaker direct impacts, suggesting more indirect roles. These findings highlight the necessity of prioritizing agility and human capital to optimize internal technology transfer.

title: Relational Alignment and Strategy Implementation How Top Manager–Middle Manager Dynamics Shape Execution
affiliations: University of Galway and University of Padua

detail.title: Relational Alignment and Strategy Implementation How Top Manager–Middle Manager Dynamics Shape Execution
detail.abstract: Strategy implementation frequently breaks down not because strategies are poorly formulated, but because they may be enacted through strained or misaligned relationships between organizational levels. Middle managers play a pivotal role in this process, translating strategic intent into operational action while navigating competing demands for compliance, adaptation, and innovation. Yet, we still lack a clear explanation of how relational dynamics between top managers and middle managers shape implementation outcomes. Drawing on a mixed-methods study of 39 Italian manufacturing firms undergoing digitalization, servitization, and sustainability transformations, this study examines how relational alignment and misalignment between top and middle managers affect strategy implementation. Combining qualitative interviews with 96 managers and survey data from 49 matched top manager–middle manager dyads, we show that high-quality relationships alone are insufficient. Instead, implementation fidelity, adaptive divergence, and innovation critically depend on whether top and middle managers share aligned perceptions of trust, openness, and reciprocity. Relational asymmetries systematically reduce middle managers’ strategic involvement, delay innovation projects, and weaken implementation outcomes. By conceptualizing strategy implementation as a relational accomplishment, this study advances implementation research by identifying relational alignment as a core mechanism linking managerial interactions to strategic outcomes. For practitioners, the findings highlight relational symmetry as a manageable condition of implementation, alongside structure, resources, and control systems.

title: Development of a Digital Safety Self-Efficacy Scale for University Students

detail.title: Development of a Digital Safety Self-Efficacy Scale for University Students
detail.abstract: While theoretical explanations of digital safety (DS) provide information about current competencies, operational definitions are essential to assess students' awareness and skills, as well as the effectiveness of educational practices. This study aimed to develop a valid and reliable scale to measure digital safety self-efficacy. To achieve this, we created an item pool, collected expert opinions, conducted a pilot test, performed factor analysis and tested to measurement invariance. The exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) involved data from 490 and 821 university students, respectively. The EFA produced a scale with 23 items measuring two factors and accounting for 56% of the total variance. Subsequently, the CFA showed that the scale had an optimal and satisfactory fit with the data. Additionally, the convergent and divergent validity results indicated that the scale demonstrated discriminant validity. The final version included 23 items and two factors, and we named it the Digital Safety Self-Efficacy Scale (DSSES). In this context, DSSES will be a valuable tool for advancing systematic research on digital safety self-efficacy and for comprehensively assessing the levels of digital safety self-efficacy among university students.

title: Similarity-Organized Append-Only Updates for Reducing Device-Level Write Amplification Under Matched Durability

detail.title: Similarity-Organized Append-Only Updates for Reducing Device-Level Write Amplification Under Matched Durability
detail.abstract: Modern storage stacks often translate small logical updates into disproportionately large physical writes due to logging, copy-on-write, and background maintenance, increasing write amplification (WA), device traffic, and operational energy. This paper introduces Model SN (Similarity Network Storage), an append-only update design in which records are written sequentially while a lightweight similarity structure (vector index / neighbor links) supports retrieval and grouping without relocating existing records. Inspired by biological self-organization as an analogy, the system is engineered and evaluated using standard storage metrics.We evaluate Model SN using a PC-based benchmark comparing it against a WAL-based baseline (SQLite) under explicitly matched durability settings (strict vs group). In the current dataset, Model SN consistently reduces device-level bytes written per logical update (Bytes/op) across tested conditions and improves throughput in strict durability, while showing a durability-batching trade-off in group settings. Ongoing replication is intended to further tighten uncertainty bounds, but current evidence already supports the conclusion that similarity-organized append-only updates can reduce unnecessary device traffic and can contribute to more sustainable data-intensive computing.

title: Smart Wards in Healthcare: A Taxonomy and Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Duisburg-Essen - Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine (IKIM), University of Duisburg-Essen - Department of Nuclear Medicine, University of Duisburg-Essen - Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine (IKIM), affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Duisburg-Essen - Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine (IKIM)

detail.title: Smart Wards in Healthcare: A Taxonomy and Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
detail.abstract: A systematic review with meta-analysis was conducted to examine the current landscape of Smart Wards and their associated technologies. A total of 55 peer-reviewed studies, published between 2000 and 2023, were included. We introduced a two-sided taxonomy categorizing Smart Wards by technological domain (sensors, assistant devices, robotics, tracking, integrated units, and extended reality) and by intended user groups such as patients, doctors, nurses, administrators, and relatives. This structured framework allows for a systematic mapping of existing use cases and illustrates how specific technologies interact with user groups across clinical contexts. The review further identifies the medical specialties in which technologies are predominantly employed. General wards, geriatrics, and surgical wards emerged as the primary specialties. Technologies such as physiological data sensors and agitation monitoring systems are particularly prevalent in geriatrics, while surgical wards often employ systems for continuous wireless monitoring and early warning. We further discussed the parts a Smart Ward is composed of in detail and provided real world examples of systems that have already been tested in clinical environments. The subsequent meta-analysis compared traditional temperature measurement methods with smart thermometry devices. The analysis, based on three prospective studies with 676 participants, revealed a slight, though not statistically significant, trend towards lower temperature readings by smart devices. Overall, the findings indicate that Smart Ward technologies offer measurable improvements in patient safety, workflow efficiency, and the personalization of care. Nevertheless, significant implementation challenges persist, notably regarding system interoperability, data security, inconsistent device standardization, and clinical staff acceptance of emerging technologies. These limitations highlight the necessity for additional research on scalable integration approaches, the long-term success of these systems, and the development of robust frameworks for ethical data handling. In particular, the combined deployment of multiple technologies within integrated Smart Ward environments remains understudied, particularly regarding their impact on clinical decision-making and the overall quality of care delivery.

title: An Intelligent Scholarship Discovery and TrackingSystemtoAssist Students in Finding and Applying for RelevantScholarships

detail.title: An Intelligent Scholarship Discovery and TrackingSystemtoAssist Students in Finding and Applying for RelevantScholarships
detail.abstract: Securing financial aid is a critical yet complexendeavor for students due to the fragmented natureof scholarship information and the risingprevalence of fraudulent listings. This researchintroduces an Intelligent Scholarship Discovery andTracking System, an AI-powered platformdesigned to streamline the end-to-end scholarshipapplication process. Unlike traditional searchengines, the proposed system employs a multi- modular approach: a User Profile Managementmodule for secure, encrypted data handling; a DataExtraction layer using Selenium for real-time webscraping; and a Rule-Based Matching Algorithm toprovide personalized recommendations. To enhance student success rates, the systemintegrates advanced features such as an AI EssayHelper for drafting application materials and aCredibility Checker to safeguard students frompredatory listings. Furthermore, the platformincorporates a Smart Application Dashboard totrack deadlines and an Opportunity Gap Finder thatidentifies missing skills required for future high- value scholarships. By combining predictiveanalytics with automated discovery, this systemreduces manual search efforts, minimizesinformation overload, and empowers students tomake data-driven decisions.

title: Electricity Sector Inefficiencies as a Carbon Footprint Amplifier: ARDL Evidence from Zambia's Hydropower-Dependent Economy
affiliations: Ankara Social Sciences University, Social Sciences University of Ankara and Social Sciences University of Ankara

detail.title: Electricity Sector Inefficiencies as a Carbon Footprint Amplifier: ARDL Evidence from Zambia's Hydropower-Dependent Economy
detail.abstract: While Zambia's hydropower-dominated electricity sector is inherently low-carbon, systemic inefficiencies function as a 'carbon footprint amplifier,' creating a vicious 'climate-carbon cycle' that threatens environmental and energy sustainability. Using an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) model on 1990–2024 time series data, we quantify these dynamics. Results show that economic growth (GDP) is the primary driver of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions; a 1% increase in GDP is associated with a 2.58% long-run and 2.22% short-run rise in CO2 emissions. Crucially, the study identifies a paradoxical dynamic whereby grid losses temporarily suppress emissions by restricting power supply, yet entrench long-term fossil-fuel reliance, a “self-damaging decarbonisation”. Conversely, increased electricity consumption reduces CO2 emissions by displacing carbon-intensive decentralised fossil fuel backups. These findings reframe grid efficiency not merely as a technical goal but as a critical climate mitigation tool in hydro-dependent economies. The study advocates for grid modernisation and carbon pricing to decouple growth from fossil-fuel dependence and break the climate-carbon cycle.

title: Comparative Analysis of China and Global Trends in the Environmental Economics of Natural Resources
affiliations: Wuhan University and Guangzhou College of Commerce

detail.title: Comparative Analysis of China and Global Trends in the Environmental Economics of Natural Resources
detail.abstract: Policymakers must prioritize the achievement of the Sustainability Development Goals (SDGs). This issue can only be resolved if the regulatory authorities redirect the tendency toward energy-led development. This Research takes into account 127 nations from 1990 to 2019 and looks at how energy imports and income from natural assets affect green growth. The empirical approach takes into account fraud, globalization, and population increase. Using the cross-sectional augmenting autoregressive distribution lag (CS-ARDL) approach, the results demonstrate that energy imports have adverse effects on ecological sustainability in both the short and long term. To a lesser extent, rents from local assets can promote eco-friendly development. In opposition to the beneficial effects of population growth and globalization, corruption hampers equitable growth. The results of the study form the basis of a sustainable development policy framework. The rules and regulations are constructed by rearranging energy imports and rent from natural assets in order to account for corruption, globalization, and increasing communities.

title: Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning algorithms for land use land cover classification and prediction of Chattogram District, Bangladesh

detail.title: Performance Evaluation of Machine Learning algorithms for land use land cover classification and prediction of Chattogram District, Bangladesh
detail.abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) change is one of the most significant factors that cause environmental degradation all over the world and has a vital impact on ecosystem structure and ecosystem functioning. This study aims to assess the spatiotemporal patterns of LULC in Chattogram District in Bangladesh and evaluate the machine learning (ML) model performance to predict future LULC. In Google Earth Engine (GEE), Landsat imagery of 2006, 2015, and 2025 was categorized into five LULC categories with the use of the Random Forest (RF) classifier with overall accuracies ranging between 90.45% to 95.96%. The LULC change detection showed significant changes between cropland, vegetation, and built-up land, representing the rapid changes in agriculture and gradual urbanization. A transition potential model and a model of the future were done with Land Change Modeler (LCM) in TerrSet on the combination of biophysical and distance-based driver variables. The overall comparison of RF and Support Vector Machine (SVM) models revealed that RF was better at overall prediction (92.63%), and thus it would be used to predict LULC in 2035 in a Markov Chain structure. The 2035 projection shows that the urban land will continue to grow (4.63% of total area), it will experience dramatic expansions of the cropland, and vegetation, waterbodies, and bare land will be reduced. This study's finding proves that machine learning-driven geospatial modeling would contribute to beneficial knowledge about the future development of land and would allow making evidence-based planning regarding sustainable development in rapidly urbanizing areas.

title: A novel online deep learning regression controller for effective real-time maximum demand reductions using battery energy storage system
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Tunku Abdul Rahman University (UTAR) - Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A novel online deep learning regression controller for effective real-time maximum demand reductions using battery energy storage system
detail.abstract: Maximum demand (MD) is the highest peak demand of all the daily peak demands over a month. Battery energy storage system (BESS) can be used and controlled appropriately to reduce the monthly maximum demands such that customers can reduce their maximum demand charges and power utility companies can defer their network reinforcement and augmentation of generating capacity. It is important to ensure that any technique employed for BESS to reduce MD is consistent and reliable in reducing every single daily peak demand to deliver the financial benefits. An online deep learning regression controller is a new control technique introduced in this paper that is different from conventional methods. This technique operates using its regression ability to generate the best possible threshold in real-time such that BESS supplies real power to the load when the load demand exceeds the threshold. This regression ability is absent in all the published BESS controllers. Its regression ability is trained with the historical data and actively updated with its new data by using its online learning feature to capture any long-term changes in the demand due to the human behavioural or climate changes. The performance of the controller is evaluated through simulation and real-world experiment. The simulation studies show that the controller achieves improved performance when benchmarked against other deep learning models and existing controllers with an average maximum demand reduction factor of 75.08%. The DLR controller achieves about 10.89% higher maximum demand reduction than the next closest contender. Furthermore, the experimental results validate its effectiveness, showing an average maximum demand reduction factor of 73.49%. Overall, the online proposed controller effectively reduces maximum demands in both simulation and real-world scenarios, achieving an improvement of 175.42% compared to a battery system with basic scheduling.

title: Congruence Effect of Family Member Ratios of the Board and Management on R&D Investments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, East China University of Science and Technology and Missouri University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Congruence Effect of Family Member Ratios of the Board and Management on R&D Investments
detail.abstract: Building on agency theory, this study posits that the family director ratio (FDR) and the family executive ratio (FER) jointly determine whether board monitoring is fitted or unfitted. When the two ratios are similar (high FDR–high FER congruence or low FDR–low FER congruence), agency costs are minimised, which engages firms to invest in research and development (R&D). When the ratios diverge, unfitted monitoring triggers either principal–agent costs (high FDR–low FER incongruence) or asymmetric altruism costs (low FDR–high FER incongruence), reducing R&D. Moreover, high family ownership exhibits a positive moderating effect on the relationship between FDR–FER congruence and R&D investment. Empirical analyses on Chinese listed firms from 2012 to 2022 support our hypotheses.Executive summaryFamily businesses often focus on “how many family members” should place in governance, but our findings show that “where” those family members are positioned—board versus management—and whether the two levels are congruent matter more. R&D investment is highest when the proportion of family members on the board is similar to the proportion in top management (i.e., FDR–FER congruence). Such congruence contributes to fitted monitoring, which aligns goals of board and management, improves information sharing, and lowers agency costs. By contrast, FDR–FER incongruence creates monitoring gaps that discourage long-term, risky projects like R&D. Besides, when the family holds high ownership, the benefits of FDR–FER congruence and the penalties of FDR–FER incongruence both become more salient. Thus, before appointing additional family executives (or directors), firms should adjust the other layer accordingly to maintain FDR–FER congruence and thus safeguard their innovation effort.

title: Monetary Policy, Firm Liquidity, and Innovation in China: Evidence from Patent Data

detail.title: Monetary Policy, Firm Liquidity, and Innovation in China: Evidence from Patent Data
detail.abstract: This paper examines the long-term non-neutrality of monetary policy in China through the innovation channel, leveraging firm-level patent data and high-frequency monetary policy shocks. Our New Keynesian model demonstrates that expansionary monetary policy significantly stimulates innovation by reducing discount rates and elevating the net present value of future innovation profits, while liquidity-rich firms exhibit amplified responses due to lower R&D adjustment costs. Empirical results reveal that a one-standard-deviation easing shock increases patent stock by 2% (3% for citation-weighted quality-adjusted measures), with effects persisting for seven years. Heterogeneity analysis underscores that private enterprises with stronger liquidity buffers drive this response, whereas state-owned enterprises remain unaffected, reflecting differences in credit access constraints. These findings challenge classical neutrality paradigms, highlighting monetary policy’s role in fostering productivity growth. Our findings suggest policymakers should target liquidity provision to high-productivity private firms and provide complementary intellectual property reforms in order to maximize long-term growth outcomes.
